title: A title or a logo laid over a video lands on a track named for what it holds
goal: The title walkthrough mock names the tracks a title and a piece of art land on by what they carry (Title, Gfx) beside V1 and Audio 1. Today a title or a logo let go on the timeline makes a new track called V2, V3 and so on, so a busy edit reads as a column of numbers instead of saying where the titles and the graphics are.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-title-wt.html steps 2 and 7 ("A Gfx track appears under the Title track carrying its clip"); the frame shows tracks Gfx, Title, V1, Audio 1. Code: PhotonzDocument.titleLanding (TitlePresetShelf.swift) names a new track freeTrackName(.video) and land(_:at:) calls addTrack(kind, at:), which names it the same way (DocumentTracks.swift ~451, ~543). Needs a name carried on ClipLanding into addTrack. Pictures land through PhotonzDocument.landPicture (PictureClip.swift), added by a-logo-or-picture-can-be-brought-into-a-video-fo. grep walks for "track": "V2" before changing.
acceptance: A title tile let go over the timeline on a new track makes a track called Title (Title 2 and on when one exists), as the mock draws it
A picture tile from the Library let go on a new track makes a track called Gfx (Gfx 2 and on)
The ghost in the air names the same track the clip lands on
Every walk that expected V2 for a title or a picture is updated in the same commit and passes

log.note: Adversarial pass: a Premiere editor names tracks by hand; auto-naming by content (Title, Gfx) beats V-numbers for reading a busy edit. Risk found: a title double-clicked at the playhead went on a track named after the preset (Title Page) while a dropped one would say Title, two names side by side in one timeline. Fixed in this task: a preset carrying its title recipe counts as a title for track naming (Layer.isTitleText), so both land on Title, Title 2.

Built: ClipLanding's trackName now names the new track land() makes (addTrack named:, falling back to the next of its kind if the name was taken meanwhile); titleLanding takes newTrackNamed (default Title), PhotonzDocument.pictureLanding uses Gfx, app components pass nil and stay V-numbered. Tests first in TitlePresetShelfTests + LibraryPictureTests. Walks updated: library-picture-import-walk (V2 -> Gfx, ghost says 'Picture · New Gfx'), title-presets-library-shelf-walk (V2 -> Title 2, Track Title Page -> Track Title). All 44 title walks, saved-name-card, an-editing-session, component-tile, paste, add-media, several-clips, empty-track-slot, new-empty-video walks green. Full suite 13,372 green (an earlier run hit the AnimatedExportWeigh flake, which passed alone and on rerun; filed an-animated-export-weighs-less-at-small-than-at). Audit pictures 1-4 checked: ghost 'Picture · New Gfx · 0:02', logo on Gfx with toast 'Acme Logo is on Gfx at 0:02', title ghost 'New Title', Title / Title 2 / V1 headers. Follow-up filed: a-title-track-and-a-gfx-track-wear-the-icons-the (header icons vs mock). Left rough, not filed: components dropped on a new track stay V-numbered (no mock names them).

Titles let go over the timeline land on a new track called Title (Title 2...), Library pictures on Gfx (Gfx 2...); the ghost says the same name; titles put in at the playhead also sit on Title. Core: ClipLanding.trackName names the new track (DocumentTracks addTrack named:, TitlePresetShelf titleLanding newTrackNamed, PictureClip pictureLanding).
